findings.issue: Nothing in the drive's state tells a writer session that is still running from one that finished. WRITER_RULE says 'Run the run: line ... in Bash, in the background; then next.' A `next` taken straight after the background launch meets, for a first dispatch, executor None plus the dispatched-executor mark and asks no-executor-return (offering resume/retry while the session runs, so a second session can be started on the same tree); for a resume round it meets a filed executor with no gated mark and runs the task gate on the session's half-written tree, which can record a spurious red and spend a resume round. The record file (session_record) is the only completion signal and advance does not consult it before deciding. ws1-ws7 play each session synchronously (_play_session) before the next `next`, so no case can see this.
findings.resolution: Make completion explicit: either word the rule 'run it in the background and take `next` only when it exits', or (better, mechanical) have advance return a `wait` step while a writer session was dispatched for the current round and its record has not appeared (and no record means not finished), and add a case that calls `next` between dispatch and the run.

findings.issue: The task reads two new config keys, executor.writerModel and executor.writerBudgetUsd, that the config schema does not know: validate-config.py prints 'WARNING: unknown executor key' for each (the executor's own NOT DONE note (a)). A key the plugin reads but its validator calls unknown is a user-visible false warning on the only way to turn the feature on.
findings.resolution: Add both keys to the config schema and _config_rules (here or in a named follow-up task) so the validator accepts what the driver reads.

findings.issue: These commands drive the same `drive-phase.py next` signal but still describe `dispatch` as 'an Agent'. Under executor.writerModel their dispatch is a `run:` line to run in background Bash, so a /audit:next or /audit:run session reading only its own command file would try an Agent call on a command line (the executor's NOT DONE note (b)). Only phase.md was in scope.
findings.resolution: Reword the dispatch step in each of those command files the way phase.md now reads, or point them at one shared sentence.

findings.issue: --record is written for every outcome including a usage refusal (prefixed `usage:`), but no case covers the usage-refusal path or an unwritable record path; only the success path is exercised, indirectly via ws2-ws6 through test_drive_phase.py (executor's NOT DONE note (d)).
findings.resolution: Add a case in tests/test_run_agent_session.py: a bad --model with --record leaves {"line": "usage: ...", "exit": 2}, and an unwritable --record changes no exit code.
